answers.label: Feedback on clarified MBM definition
answers.text:
We do not agree that this definition should be made mandatory; instead, we suggest that it be made optional.
See our responses in Section 5.

answers.label: Feedback on stated purposes of the MBM
answers.text:
We do not agree. We would appreciate clarification as to why abatement planning, target setting, and policy engagement are included, as these elements do not relate to market-based GHG reporting and appear to go beyond the intended scope of the GHG Protocol. These elements are not related to historical, realized GHG reporting.

Furthermore, for the majority of companies, no market-based mechanisms have been used to date. As a result, their location-based and market-based reporting currently yields the same outcome.

answers.label: Reasons against QC4 hourly matching
selections: Hourly matching should follow an optional ‘may’ rather than a required ‘shall’ approach
Concern that requiring hourly matching does not create meaningful improvements to inventory accuracy
Concern that a requirement for hourly contractual instruments could discourage global participation in voluntary clean energy procurement markets

answers.label: Comments on opposition to QC4
answers.text:
We would be comfortable with this being an option; however, we would not support it being made mandatory.
But be aware this could slow overall decarbonization and clean energy investment and may disadvantage emerging economies, where electricity grids are often more emissions intensive. In addition, it would significantly increase complexity. Overall, this would not make GHG reporting easier, but rather more complicated, without making the information more useful for report users.

answers.label: Why that US boundary upholds deliverability
answers.text: We would appreciate clarification as to why specific guidance for the United States is included, given that the GHG Protocol is intended to function as a global standard.

answers.label: Why the alternative threshold fits better
answers.text: As we recommend that the use of these principles should not be mandatory, we therefore consider that no threshold should be applied.
